name: A rumour
description: What people are saying, and sometimes what is actually true.

tables.name: A rumour
tables.description: Roll it when the party asks around.

entries.body: A caravan is three days late and nobody will say why.
The well on the east side has gone sweet, and it was never sweet.
Somebody is buying up boats, quietly, for more than they are worth.
The mayor has not been seen in a week. The mayor's coach has.
A child went missing and came back with a different accent.
There is a new tax coming, on doors.
The guard captain lost at cards to a stranger and paid in a key.
Lights on the hill, three nights running, where the old fort was.
The priest has stopped ringing the dawn bell and will not say why.
A ship came in flying no flag and left flying two.
Somebody is asking after the party by name.
The river is running the wrong way at the bend, for an hour each morning.
The baker's dog will not go near the cellar any more.
A wedding was called off at the altar, and the groom left town on foot.
The old bridge is to be pulled down, and the new one is not built.
There is a reward posted, but the notice was torn down before anyone read it.
A soldier came home from a war nobody has heard of.
The fishmonger has started paying in old coin.
Somebody has been sleeping in the graveyard, and tidying it.
The letters from the capital have stopped.
A wolf was seen in the market square at noon, and it was not hungry.
A house on the high street has been empty a year and last night it had a light in it.
The healer will not treat anyone from the north bank.
The party has been talked about, favourably, by somebody important.

tables.name: A rumour: and the truth of it
tables.description: For the GM's eyes. What is behind it, if anything.

entries.body: The truth: it is exactly as they say, and worse.
The truth: it is a lie, spread on purpose, and the party has just met the person spreading it.
The truth: it was true a month ago and is over now, and the ending is the story.
The truth: it is two separate things, told as one.
The truth: it is true, and the person who told the party is part of it.
The truth: nobody knows, and the not knowing is what is doing the damage.
The truth: it is a cover for something smaller and more embarrassing.
The truth: it is a cover for something larger, and the cover is failing.
The truth: a child started it, and adults finished it.
The truth: it is true, and the authorities know, and they are waiting.
The truth: it is half true, and the wrong half is the one people repeat.
The truth: it is about the party, and they do not know it yet.
